svg.title: Four Questions Before Acquisition Cash Leaves Escrow
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-acquisition-statutory-risk-decisions; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Questions Before Acquisition Cash Leaves Escrow; subtitle: Proceed on evidence; cure or reject material unresolved defects; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Read the four nodes sequentially. An affirmative, documented finding advances to the next node; an adverse or incomplete finding routes to a documented cure or rejection before closing. Federal environmental rules and California statutory examples serve different purposes; apply the actual property's state and local requirements rather than exporting California rules.; caption: Title insurance, a clean-looking map, and a low purchase price answer different questions. None independently establishes legal access, permitted use, environmental suitability, or authority to represent another seller.; stages: label: Title and access; value: Document rights or stop; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Review vesting, liens, taxes, recorded easements, surveys, and commitment exceptions with the title provider and counsel. Require access rights adequate for the intended use; cure defects before closing or reject the parcel rather than assume coverage.; label: Zoning and legal division; value: Confirm the lawful parcel; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Obtain jurisdiction-specific findings on legal-lot status, setbacks, minimum area, and proposed division. For California examples, review Government Code §§ 66424 and 66428 and applicable local ordinances; an assessor parcel identifier alone proves no split approval.; label: Environmental constraints; value: Investigate before taking title; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Evaluate contamination under 42 U.S.C. § 9607 and applicable inquiry requirements under 40 CFR Part 312. Check flood exposure and potential jurisdictional waters; discharges of dredged or fill material may require authorization under 33 U.S.C. § 1344.; label: Representation and disclosures; value: Verify role and offering rules; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Distinguish owned-inventory sales from compensated representation of others. California examples include Business and Professions Code §§ 10130–10131 for licensing and § 11010 for covered subdivided-land offerings. Verify exemptions, required reports, and property-specific disclosures before solicitation or sale.

Check flood exposure and potential jurisdictional waters; discharges of dredged or fill material may require authorization under 33 U.S.C. § 1344.
